newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares close near highs helped by futures.
newsitem.headline: German shares close near highs helped by futures.

text.p: German shares, shrugging off the directionless mood of the last few days, closed higher in bourse trade on Friday as the knock-on effect of the expiry of DAX futures exerted a positive influence.

The DAX index of 30 blue chip shares closed 21.66 points or 0.83 percent higher at 2,646.10, just off a new record intra-day high of 2,650.49, as stronger German Bunds and an ever-firmer dollar supported prices.
But dealers remarked that turnover was small and likely to remain so before the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting to consider U.S. interest rates next week.

"From the client side, trade is pretty thin. It looks as if most of it is coming from the derivatives side," one said, noting that money invested in the futures market was now being transfered to the cash market.
The December DAX future contract traded 15.5 points up at 2,659.5 after the expiry of the September contract.

Electronics group Siemens AG, finishing up 53 pfennigs at 79.25 marks, was seen as benefitting from the stronger U.S. currency and the firm performance of U.S. high-tech stocks on Wall Street Thursday night amid a mixed overall market.
Export-led stocks such as Bayer AG, Hoechst AG and BASF AG in the chemicals sector all gained on the dollar's strength, as did vehicle-maker Daimler-Benz AG, up 88 pfennnigs at 84.03.

Traders said Daimler also benefitted from positive comments coming from the Hannover truck fair, where its Mercedes-Benz unit indicated it was confident of record sales in its commercial vehicle side.
But in reference to the overall market, they added that the so-called "triple-witching' expiry of options and futures due on Wall Street Friday could produce swings in German electronic trade later.
